title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief: Your docs chatbot answers questions about Acme's API. The model was trained before the current docs were written, so it answers from memory: most numbers are out of date, and none come with a source. Support rejects any answer without a source link. Answer at least 85% of questions correctly with a citation, for under $0.03 per question.

tasks.label: Refund window
tasks.prompt: How many days do customers have to request a refund?

tasks.label: Rate limit
tasks.prompt: What is the API rate limit on the Pro plan?

tasks.label: SSO
tasks.prompt: Can I use SSO on the Team plan?

tasks.label: Not in the docs
tasks.prompt: Do you have a native SAP integration?

retrieve.text: Retriever: embedded the question, top chunks by cosine: billing.md#refunds (0.83), limits.md#pro (0.61), plans.md#sso (0.58). Pasted into the prompt with their source ids.

retrieve_one.text: Retriever: top 1 chunk by cosine: changelog.md#2025-03 (0.71). It mentions the topic but not the answer.

retrieve_flood.text: Retriever: top chunks by cosine, all pasted in: 20 chunks from billing.md, limits.md, plans.md, changelog.md, faq.md ... (40,000 tokens)

memory_wrong.text: From what I know: refunds within 30 days, 1,000 requests per minute on Pro, and SSO on every plan. (Training data. All three are out of date.)

memory_uncited.text: I'm fairly sure about this, but I can't point you to a page. (No citation: support can't verify it, so the answer is rejected.)

invent.text: Yes, Acme has a native SAP integration under Settings → Integrations. (It does not. The model filled the gap.)

not_found.text: I couldn't find an SAP integration in the docs. The integrations page lists Salesforce, HubSpot and Zapier [integrations.md#list]. Want me to connect you with sales?

wrong_chunk.text: According to the changelog, this changed in March 2025 [changelog.md#2025-03]. (The cited chunk does not actually contain the answer.)

cited_refund.text: Customers can request a refund within 14 days of the charge [billing.md#refunds].

cited_rate.text: The Pro plan allows 600 requests per minute per API key; bursts over that get HTTP 429 [limits.md#pro].

cited_sso.text: No. SAML SSO is included on the Business plan and above, not Team [plans.md#sso].

modifiers.note: With nothing to look at, the model fills the gap.
The answer is in the prompt, with a source id to cite.
One chunk: when the top hit is wrong, there is no second chance.
Twenty chunks: the right one is buried in the middle.
Nothing relevant came back, so the grounded answer is 'not in the docs'.

goals.label: At least 85% correct, with a citation

hints: The model is answering from what it learned in training. Where are the current docs in this graph?
Add a Retriever and wire it into the Model, so the top chunks land in the prompt with their source ids.
Retriever → Model with Top k between 3 and 5. Top k of 1 misses too often; 20 floods the prompt and costs about $0.13 a question.
explain: RAG puts the right text in front of the model before it answers, so it stops relying on training data and can point to its source. Top k is the dial: too few chunks miss the answer, too many bury it and multiply the bill.
